evals.name: empty-args-routes-to-deepening
evals.expected_output: Empty args route to the deepening lens (not a missing-action error). Reads the nearest project glossary (if any) and relevant architecture decision records, walks the codebase via the Explore subagent, applies the deletion test, and writes BOTH the HTML report and the machine-readable candidate artifact before asking which candidate to explore.
expectations: Routes empty `$ARGUMENTS` to the `deepening` action — does NOT error on a missing/unknown action
Reads the nearest project glossary (if the project maintains one) and any relevant architecture decision records before exploring
Uses the Agent tool with subagent_type=Explore (or an equivalent read-only exploration subagent) to walk the codebase rather than reading inline
Applies the deletion test to anything suspected shallow (concentrates vs moves complexity)

Writes the durable machine-readable candidate artifact to the memory tier (default `.work/<topic-slug>/deepening-candidates-<timestamp>.md`, honoring a working-docs root the consuming repo declares, with the path announced) alongside the HTML report
Does NOT propose interfaces in Phase 2; ends by asking which candidate to explore

evals.name: shallow-cluster-classified-strong
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve deepening — focus on the order intake path: OrderHandler calls OrderValidator calls OrderRepo, and each is a one-method wrapper that forwards its argument and returns the next call's result. Validation and pricing logic actually live spread across the three.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the OrderHandler->OrderValidator->OrderRepo chain as shallow (interface nearly as complex as implementation). Deletion test returns 'concentrates'. Recommendation badge Strong, dependency category in-process or local-substitutable with the testing strategy tied to it. Candidate written to the candidate artifact with status proposed.
expectations: Identifies the wrapper chain as shallow — interface nearly as complex as the implementation
Deletion-test verdict is 'concentrates complexity' (earning-its-keep / candidate signal), not 'just moves it'
Assigns the recommendation badge Strong for an unambiguous shallow pass-through cluster
Assigns a dependency category (in-process or local-substitutable) and ties the testing strategy to that category per dependencies.md
Uses ONLY deepening vocabulary (module, interface, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) — never component, service, or boundary
Records the candidate in the candidate artifact with status: proposed and a one-sentence problem + one-sentence deepening

evals.name: deep-module-not-over-flagged
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve deepening — review the pricing engine: a single Price(order) entry point backed by ~600 lines of rules, tax tables, and rounding policy, with a focused test suite that drives it only through Price(order). An architecture decision record already records keeping the rules in-process.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT propose deepening an already-deep module (small interface, large well-tested implementation). Deletion test shows complexity would only move, not concentrate. If surfaced at all, badge is Speculative with explicit rationale; respects the existing decision record rather than re-litigating it.
expectations: Does NOT recommend deepening a module that is already deep (small interface hiding large, tested behavior)
Deletion-test verdict is 'would just move complexity' — correctly NOT a candidate
If surfaced at all, badge is Speculative with explicit rationale — never Strong
Respects the existing architecture decision record (keep rules in-process); only revisits it if friction is real enough, and marks the conflict clearly if so
Does not invent shallowness where the interface-to-implementation ratio is already favorable

evals.name: design-it-twice-branch-on-selected-candidate
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve deepening — I've picked the order intake candidate from the report. Before we lock a shape, show me a few radically different interface designs and tell me which one you'd pick.
evals.expected_output: Enters the Design-It-Twice exploration mode: frames the problem space (constraints, dependency categories, an illustrative sketch labeled not-a-proposal) and shows it to the user first, fans out 3-4 parallel subagents each under a deliberately orthogonal design constraint, presents the six-part designs sequentially, compares on interface depth/leverage, locality of change, and seam placement, reads what the spread of designs itself says, and closes with an opinionated recommendation (hybrid allowed, carrying a graft record).
expectations: Frames the problem space FIRST — constraints any new interface must satisfy, dependency categories, and a small illustrative sketch explicitly labeled as not a proposal — and shows it to the user before any design is produced

Fans out 3-4 subagents in parallel, each under a deliberately orthogonal design constraint (minimal interface, maximum flexibility, optimize the common caller, ports and adapters only when cross-seam dependencies warrant)

Briefs each subagent with the concrete technical context (file paths, coupling details, dependency category, what the seam hides) and requires the six-part structured result (interface incl. invariants/error modes; usage example; what the implementation hides; dependency strategy; trade-offs; rejected shapes with their rejected-reason)
Presents the designs sequentially, then compares on exactly three axes: interface depth/leverage, locality of change, and seam placement

Reads the spread of returns as evidence: convergence despite orthogonal constraints is treated as a strong consensus signal, divergence in shape is treated as the expected null result rather than a reason to re-frame, and divergence in the designs' assumptions about callers/invariants/ordering sends step 1's framing back to be pinned
Closes with an opinionated recommendation — possibly a hybrid — a strong read, not a menu of equally weighted options
Any proposed hybrid carries a graft record: what was taken from which design, and what was considered and left behind with its reason

evals.name: resolved-vocabulary-routes-to-owner
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve deepening — while grilling the selected candidate we resolved a new project term, Fulfillment Window. /domain-driven-design:curate-language is available in this session. Preserve the term and continue.
evals.expected_output: Invokes /domain-driven-design:curate-language for active glossary maintenance, then resumes the architecture interview. Architecture does not duplicate the glossary contract or discover bounded contexts; when that skill is unavailable it preserves only the consumer-owned fallback.
expectations: Invokes /domain-driven-design:curate-language because the skill is available in the current session
Does not reimplement a glossary filename, location, or entry contract in architecture
Does not perform bounded-context discovery as part of preserving the term
Continues the selected-candidate interview after the glossary update

evals.name: multi-candidate-handoff-stops-before-implementation
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve deepening — the report is out. Take candidates 2, 5 and 7, agree their shapes with me, then hand them off together. Candidate 5 renames the public helper load_config to read_config.
evals.expected_output: Interviews each selected candidate to its own agreed shape and implements none of them. Before the handoff it re-runs the base-freshness check and reports the behind count. The handoff records the landing order and why, the files two or more candidates touch, and which candidates depend on another landing first, leaving commit granularity and PR shape to the implementing lane. It states that a suite skipped for a missing tool is not a pass and a stub is not the tool, and that retiring load_config sweeps call sites, comments, and test assertions, keeping changelog history entries that record the old name.
expectations: Interviews candidates 2, 5 and 7 one at a time, each to its own agreed shape
Does NOT implement any candidate or offer an implement-all mode; stops at the handoff
Re-checks the branch's freshness against its base before handing off and reports the behind count
The handoff names landing order with rationale, file overlaps between the candidates, and inter-candidate dependencies
The handoff states that a skipped suite is not a pass and a stub is not the tool
The handoff's rename step for load_config covers comments and test assertions as well as call sites, and exempts changelog history passages

evals.name: report-bands-by-badge-and-artifact-records-verification
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve deepening — scope is the whole repository, which splits into four top-level packages. Run the scan through to the report.
evals.expected_output: Before scanning, checks the branch against its base with separate git calls and reports the behind count. It names four scan subagents, one per package, before dispatching, and notes that scan cost rises with the count; no fixed default width is asserted. The HTML report groups cards into Strong, Worth exploring, and Speculative bands in that order, with no cap, pagination, or collapsed card. The candidate artifact ends with a phase-1.5 line carrying downgraded, dropped, and corrected counts, then the top-recommendation line, and leaves agreed-shape and graft-record out of entries that have not reached Phase 3.
expectations: Runs the base-freshness check as separate git calls before the scan and reports the behind count or an unknown freshness
Dispatches one scan subagent per package and names the count and areas before dispatching, without citing a fixed default fan-out number
Renders cards in badge bands ordered Strong, Worth exploring, Speculative, with no cap, pagination, or collapsed disclosure
The candidate artifact carries a phase-1.5 line with downgraded, dropped, and corrected counts, even when all are zero
Does not leave empty agreed-shape or graft-record fields on entries that have not reached Phase 3

evals.name: boundaries-recorded-rule-crossing-handed-on
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve boundaries. We are on branch feature/billing-split. ARCHITECTURE.md line 14 says "Billing.Reports must not reference Billing.Ledger directly." The architecture topic doc declares architecture_dir: docs/architecture, and docs/architecture/dependency-graph.json is current and has a resolved project edge from src/Billing.Reports/Billing.Reports.csproj to src/Billing.Ledger/Billing.Ledger.csproj. When you show me the crossing I will confirm the rule for enforcement.
evals.expected_output: Reads the 'Where boundary rules live' list from the enforcement-ladder copy, records the ARCHITECTURE.md rule with its source line, reads the existing dependency graph, and reports the Reports-to-Ledger edge as a crossing citing both the rule's source line and the edge's manifest evidence. After the user confirms, it writes one review-findings file under .work/improve/feature-billing-split/ (after checking that the memory root carries a .gitignore with *), with the rule as a row under an architecture dimension heading, names that file in the report, and offers /corrections:codify findings on it without running it.
expectations: Takes the rule sources from the 'Where boundary rules live' list in the enforcement-ladder copy rather than a list of its own
Reports the src/Billing.Reports to src/Billing.Ledger edge as crossing the rule, citing ARCHITECTURE.md:14 and the manifest declaration the edge's evidence names
Writes the findings file under .work/improve/feature-billing-split/ and not under .work/reviews/
The findings file has type: review-findings frontmatter and places the confirmed rule's row under a '### architecture' heading
Names the findings file in the report and offers /corrections:codify findings <file> without invoking it
Writes no architecture test and edits no source file

evals.name: boundaries-no-rules-asks-instead-of-inferring
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve boundaries. This repository has no REVIEW.md, no ARCHITECTURE.md, no ADRs, no docs/architecture folder, no unscoped rules files and no architecture-test configuration. It has three projects: src/Web, src/Orders and src/Shared, and Web references Orders, which references Shared.
evals.expected_output: Says that no boundary rule is recorded and names the sources it checked. Collects the edges through the plugin's dependency map, presents the three internal edges, and asks the user which reference directions must never occur. It proposes no rule from the folder names or the existing references, and writes no findings file because no rule has been confirmed.
expectations: States that no boundary rule is recorded and names the sources from the 'Where boundary rules live' list that it checked
Generates the dependency graph with --out under .work/improve/<branch-slug>/, after checking that the memory root carries a .gitignore with *, and writes no file into a tracked directory
Presents the Web to Orders and Orders to Shared edges and asks which directions are forbidden
Does not propose a boundary rule from the folder names or from the references that exist today
Writes no findings file, because no rule has been confirmed

evals.name: split-ownership-cites-open-file-test
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve deepening — focus on the cart area: CartService and CheckoutService each assign cart.discountCode directly, and PromoBanner keeps its own copy of the code that it refreshes on a timer. Nothing documents that the three must agree.
evals.expected_output: Scans the cart area and returns a split-ownership candidate: three places write or copy the same state (cart.discountCode), so an agent that edits one writer cannot see the others. The candidate cites the open-file test (with only the file being edited open, an agent cannot see every other place it must change; the answer is no) in its shallow-signal, and names the remedy of one owner per piece of state with the others reading it or asking the owner. Uses the deepening vocabulary.
expectations: Names split ownership as the hazard: more than one module writes the same state or keeps its own copy
Cites the open-file test in the candidate's shallow-signal, and states that a no (an agent editing one writer cannot see the others) confirms the hazard
Names CartService, CheckoutService and PromoBanner as the places involved
Names the remedy as one owner per piece of state, with the others reading it or asking the owner
Uses ONLY deepening vocabulary — never component, service, or boundary — apart from the identifiers in the code

evals.name: conventions-proposes-and-writes-nothing-without-yes
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve conventions. The repository has no paved-path index and no recorded boundary rules. Under src/Orders/Handlers there are five classes, each implementing IRequestHandler<TRequest> and registered in src/Orders/Startup.cs. Show me what conventions you find; I have not decided which to keep yet.
evals.expected_output: Reads the recorded sources first and says none hold a rule or paved path. Derives the request-handler building block from the five handlers, reproduces it against the cited files, and presents it as a proposed rule with its instances, its kind and its route (a paved-path entry to /discipline:reuse-or-replace). It asks which proposals to record and, with no yes given, writes no file and invokes no other skill.
expectations: Checks the boundary-rule sources from the enforcement ladder's 'Where boundary rules live' list and the standards index for a paved-path row before deriving anything, and names what it checked
Presents the request-handler building block as a proposal citing the handler files as path:line instances
Names the proposal's route as a paved-path entry for /discipline:reuse-or-replace
Asks which proposals to record
Writes no file and invokes no other skill, because the user has not said yes to any proposal

evals.name: conventions-boundary-rule-to-architecture-concern-file
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve conventions. The convention home resolves to docs/conventions and docs/conventions/architecture/README.md exists with an architecture_dir key and no Boundary rules section. Billing.Ledger.Data is referenced only by Billing.Ledger: Billing.Ledger.csproj line 9 and no other project manifest references it. When you propose a rule for it, I say yes.
evals.expected_output: Proposes the owner rule as a boundary rule in the forbidden-reference form (every project other than Billing.Ledger must not reference Billing.Ledger.Data), with its manifest evidence. On the yes it announces the path, appends a ## Boundary rules section to docs/conventions/architecture/README.md holding one entry with the rule, its evidence and the date, leaves the YAML block and other prose unchanged, reads the file back and reports the line, and points at /architecture:improve boundaries.
expectations: Classifies the rule as a boundary rule and states it in the forbidden-reference form: no project other than Billing.Ledger references Billing.Ledger.Data
Writes only after the user's yes, announcing docs/conventions/architecture/README.md before the write
Appends a '## Boundary rules' section with one entry carrying the rule, its evidence and the date
Changes nothing outside that section: the architecture_dir key and the surrounding prose are untouched
Reads the file back, reports the line the rule landed on, and names /architecture:improve boundaries as the next step

evals.name: conventions-divergence-routed-to-codify
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve conventions. docs/standards/paved-paths.md, the file the standards index's paved-path row points at, records that OrderStore in src/Orders/OrderStore.cs is the one writer of order.status. src/Shipping/ShipmentJob.cs:42 and src/Billing/RefundService.cs:77 also assign order.status. /corrections:codify is available. When you propose handing this on, I say yes.
evals.expected_output: Lists the recorded OrderStore entry as already recorded and does not propose it again. Reports the two other writers as a divergence from it, citing both lines and the entry's source, and on the yes invokes /corrections:codify through the Skill tool with a description naming the convention and the departing places. It writes no check, no rule and no paved-path entry itself.
expectations: Lists the OrderStore owner entry as already recorded, citing docs/standards/paved-paths.md, and does not propose it again
Reports ShipmentJob.cs:42 and RefundService.cs:77 as a divergence from the recorded owner
On the yes, invokes /corrections:codify through the Skill tool with a description naming the convention, its source and both departing places
Writes no check, no boundary rule and no paved-path entry itself

evals.name: conventions-paved-path-routed-to-reuse-or-replace
evals.prompt: /architecture:improve conventions. History shows three feature commits, a1b2c3d 'feat: add refunds', d4e5f6a 'feat: add returns' and 0789abc 'feat: add exchanges', each adding a request, a handler, a validator and a migration in one commit. /discipline:reuse-or-replace is available. When you propose the feature blueprint, I say yes.
evals.expected_output: Derives the feature blueprint from the three commits, cited by hash and subject, and proposes it as a paved-path entry. On the yes it drafts the entry (the concern, the chosen way as a pointer to the commit that best shows it, the four building blocks, unordered since each feature came in one commit, and the enforcing check or none) and hands it to /discipline:reuse-or-replace through the Skill tool, writing no paved-path entry itself.
expectations: Cites the three commits by hash and subject as the blueprint's evidence
Classifies the blueprint as a paved-path entry, not a boundary rule
Drafts the entry with the concern, a pointer to the chosen way, the four building blocks without claiming an order, and the enforcing check or none
Hands the draft to /discipline:reuse-or-replace through the Skill tool and writes no paved-path entry or standards file itself
